exercises.title: Count Up with range()
description: Print the numbers 1 through 5, each on its own line — the same
task an earlier while-loop exercise solved, but this time
using a for loop with range().
<pre>> python program.py
5
range(1, 6) produces the numbers 1 through 5 — note
that the second number is where range() stops,
not the last number it includes. A for loop then runs its
body once for each value range() produces, without you having
to manage a counter variable by hand.
starter: # TODO: use a for loop with range(1, 6) to print 1 through 5

exercises.title: Count Down with a Negative Step
description: Read an integer n and print the numbers from
n down to 1, one per line, using a for loop.
<pre>> python program.py
1
range() can take a third argument, the step
— range(n, 0, -1) counts down from n to 1,
decreasing by 1 each time.

exercises.title: Countdown Then Liftoff
description: Read an integer n, count down from n to 1,
one number per line, and then print Liftoff! on its own
line after the loop finishes.
<pre>> python program.py
Liftoff!
The print("Liftoff!") line belongs after the
loop, not inside it — indentation is what decides whether a line
runs once per loop pass, or just once after the whole loop ends.
